rust.role: native control/audio/video/data and trusted composition boundary

node.role: managed helper or explicit HTTP control; bounded programmatic media through helper

python.role: async context-managed client; separately named optional sync adapter, managed helper or explicit HTTP control

browser.role: canonical WT or WSS/WebRTC, capability detection, separate device capture/render

remaining: Runtime implementation, complete per-language event/result validation, migration, conformance and exact installed-package exercises remain assigned G6-060 through G6-070.
Publisher identity, package manifests and release version require G6-069 checks; registry lookup is neither reservation nor ownership. Publication remains separately authorized.

operation_scope.record_id: opaque SDK-managed correlation, never a public authority

operation_semantics.mutation_await: Returns an observable Operation; does not wait for workflow completion.
operation_semantics.completion: Explicit wait with finite timeout returns Completion<T>.
operation_semantics.ready: Explicit waitUntilReady observes state only; no decoded-media assertion.
operation_semantics.reference: referenceJson emits versioned JSON containing original logical ID, command and scope; no secrets. Restore checks schema, command-kind witness, scope and bounded IDs before creating a local status-only handle. Expected command is saved intent, not an invented server echo.
operation_semantics.restoration: SDK-owned OperationKinds cover all 22 mapped mutation commands; a foreign kind or mismatched saved command refuses. recover accepts an existing typed reference. Neither restore nor recover submits a mutation or performs network I/O.
operation_semantics.status_fields: Current canonical operation.updated sends operation_id, optional record_id, state, revision, optional result/problem. Cancellation/expiry observations stay absent unless authoritative data actually supplies them.
operation_semantics.scope: Creating conversations and trusted provisioning may be unscoped. Retain only original asserted scopes; do not invent a Conversation parent.
operation_semantics.decision_receipts: Preserve target_operation_id, state_at_decision, disposition and optional evidence_id. Target submission assertions and the separate decision receipt scope differ: the current decision record carries original cid/sid but no connid. Its status reference must use the decision receipt scope, not copy the target Connection assertion.
operation_semantics.decision_target: DecisionReceipt.target is the authoritative target OperationId, not a fabricated original OperationKey. The current receipt does not echo target command/scope, so a freshly restored decision cannot claim those fields.
operation_semantics.decision_extensions: Typed cancel/reconcile refuse nonempty extensions until the installed durable action model includes them in intent identity; no silent discard.

revision_families.session: SessionSnapshot.revision is the observed state_revision, not a command precondition.
revision_families.topology: Session accept/reject/cancel/update/end and existing-Session invite, plus consultation/handoff/return/device move. SessionDecision.topology_revision adapts DecisionOutcome.revision. Current TransitionCompletion.session_revision is also this family.
revision_families.conversation: Participant add/update/remove and conversation-scoped handoff role assertion
revision_families.stream: current native stream controls/subscriptions; absent from a journal Connection observation until negotiated/confirmed, never guessed from its resource revision

wire_rules.private_send: message.send with cid only, nonempty Participant audience and original message ID
wire_rules.session_lifecycle: cid and sid, no connid; invite medium uses voice/video/voice+video/screen-share/text-chat/mixed, not audio
wire_rules.session_invite: an empty to list permits the canonical single-Participant Session; private sends remain nonempty
wire_rules.participant_admission: explicit identity_id, kind and role; expected Conversation revision
wire_rules.topology: all retained/admitted/retired outcomes are preserved; optional Conversation revision preserved
wire_rules.create: uses configured tenant; convenience identity list maps to initial_participants with participant role and current canonical policy defaults

contract_proofs.typed_event_boundary: Journal envelope retains source, actor, original audience and scoped IDs. Specialized incoming invitations carry public Session handles. Kind-specific payload validation follows current protocol events and the shared event matrix; advanced payload/extension data is Json.
contract_proofs.media_boundary: Stream refresh exposes current owned negotiated format/direction/clock and ownership when available; missing metadata cannot be synthesized from capability advertisement. Platform frame IO/capture/renderer implementations remain G6-050/G6-061/062/063.

review_corrections: Revision2: G6-060 Store-source audit corrects the revision1 assignment of Session command preconditions. Both general Session control and pending invitation decisions compare/increment sessions.topology_revision, independently of state_revision. No server compatibility/downgrade or alternate revision acceptance is added.

review_corrections.correction: Connection.update returns the captured ConnectionUpdateReceipt; stream subscribe/unsubscribe return StreamSelectionReceipt with explicitly nullable historical captures, not invented Stream handles. Typed stream/Participant selector sets and optional codec stream targets match the current canonical intent. Connection.end requires its reason and an optional native StreamRevision. All three target declarations and operation witnesses use these results. Observations never grant physical custody.

review_corrections.source: Canonical original-peer ICE restart and historical receipt recovery
review_corrections.correction: Add browser same-peer restartIce and a historical IceRestart connection-update outcome across Rust/Node/Python/browser decoders. The ICE counter is independent of media revisions/ownership generations. Status restoration never allocates RTC, changes owned gates/bindings or resubmits a transport effect. Browser mutation retains exact original SDP and application promises; network/media qualification remains explicit.

Expose the existing same-peer ICE restart/recovery through BrowserVideoSession without replacing capture, transceivers or its encoded-video worker. A captured ICE receipt remains separate from decoded audio/video readiness.

existing_session_invitation.inputs: Nonempty current Conversation Participants, current media, unchanged original intent/capability offer and explicit topology revision.
existing_session_invitation.incoming_outline: An accepted Session can have a newly invited Participant; only terminal Session states are skipped locally. Current actor appearance and authorization are checked by the server.

webrtc_ice_restart.result: Historical WebRtcIceRestartReceipt containing operationId, iceGeneration, streamRevision and connectionGeneration; not decoded-media readiness.
webrtc_ice_restart.other_targets: Decode historical ConnectionUpdateOutcome::IceRestart / kind:ice-restart without native media allocation. Mutation requires the original canonical WSS/WebRTC owner; native QUIC/WT and HTTP cannot substitute.
webrtc_ice_restart.recovery: Same original operation, gathered offer, peer and description-application promises. Unknown cannot create a replacement attempt. Standard operation restoration remains current-authorized metadata only.
webrtc_ice_restart.browser_video: BrowserVideoSession.restartIce(operationId, expectedStreamRevision, expectedIceGeneration, requestOptions) delegates to its same original audio/video owner; savedIceRestart preserves its original recovery snapshot.
